content.text:
Slice 2 is implemented and all four gates pass. Nothing is committed yet; I'm waiting for your review. Only `Makefile` and `tests/test_rbtree.c` changed (+176 / −6). The full test-file diff is in the output above, and the Makefile diff is earlier.

**What changed:**
- **`--stress N`** in `tests/test_rbtree.c`:
  - It builds an N-node tree on the main thread and checks it before handing it over: size, `rb_validate`, the parent-link/order checker and the spine length.
  - It then runs the operations under test on a thread whose stack is confirmed at exactly 64 KB:
    - **balanced:** `rb_foreach`, then `rb_destroy`;
    - **left-only chain:** `rb_destroy` only, as agreed.
  - After the thread joins, it checks that nothing called `rb_malloc` and that every value's destructor ran exactly once. It reports missed and repeated destructor calls separately.
  - It covers heap and pooled modes, with 34 assertions in total.
  - A malformed argument prints usage and exits with code 2; I tried 7 bad forms.
  - Running the binary with no arguments behaves as before, still with 1374 heap and 1350 pooled PASS lines (gap 24).
- **`Makefile`:**
  - `SAN_FLAGS` is now defined once and used by both `asan` and `stress-asan`. The expanded `asan` compile line is unchanged.
  - The unit test binary now links with `-pthread`.
  - `make test` runs `--stress 20000`, so `make asan` exercises the thread harness under ASan on every run.
  - New `stress-asan` target: a clean rebuild with ASan/UBSan through the same clean-then-sub-make pattern, then `--stress 1000000`.
  - `make memcheck` adds a fourth valgrind run, `--stress 20000`.

**Gate results** (from a clean build each time):

| Gate | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| `git diff --check` | clean | |
| `make test` | All tests passed; stress N=20000 passed; fuzzer 10⁵ ops in each mode OK | 1.9 s |
| `make asan` | Same as `make test`, built with `-fsanitize=address,undefined`, no reports | 6.2 s |
| `make stress-asan` | `--stress 1000000` passed: 34 PASS, 0 FAIL, foreach visited all 10⁶ keys in order, 0 missed and 0 repeated destructor calls in all 4 cases | 5.8 s |
| `make memcheck` | 4 valgrind runs, each 0 errors and "All heap blocks were freed". The stress run made 120,484 allocations and freed all of them | 6.5 s |

**Control check:** in a scratch copy I replaced `rb_destroy` with a recursive version and ran the real harness. ASan reported `stack-overflow` in `rec_free` at both N = 20,000 and N = 10⁶, on the left-only chain, after the balanced case had passed. So the routine `make test` size already catches recursion, and the balanced shape alone would not have.

**Changes beyond the reviewed design:**
1. **Line-buffered output in stress mode.** The control check showed that when output goes to a file or pipe, an ASan abort lost every PASS line, so the log didn't show which case crashed. One `setvbuf` call, in `--stress` mode only, fixes that. The crash log now ends at "[stress left spine] thread stack set to exactly 64 KB" followed by the ASan report.
2. **Two small fixes found by re-reading:** a summary `printf` that would have passed the wrong integer type in the failure case, and a "hit-counter array allocated" message that didn't say which shape it was for.

**Proposed commit message:** `M3: 10^6-node 64KB-stack teardown stress harness (--stress, stress-asan)`

After the commit, the DEVLOG entry (Φ = 2N − S proof, both slices, the scratch control results) and the CLAUDE.md updates are what's left for Evening 7. CLAUDE.md needs the 1374/1350 counts, the new commands and the four-run memcheck.

input.command:
cat >> DEVLOG.md <<'EOF'

## 2026-10-12 (HW2 Mutation 3 / M3 evening 7 — O(1)-space teardown: proof, tests, 10^6-node stress)
STATE: M2 was complete and green (`3d1afa9`, `36f82d1`, `2dc65e3`; Makefile serialization `bdbb900`). `rb_destroy` already used the HW1-era right-spine "Reach" loop; `rb_foreach` is still recursive. The question tonight was not "implement O(1) teardown" but "is the existing one correct, can I prove it terminates, and do the tests actually show it is non-recursive?" — with an explicit rule not to redesign it (e.g. into pointer reversal) unless a correctness defect turned up. None did.
DID: (1) **Review, no production change.** Traced every pointer assignment in `rb_destroy`. Free branch: `next = cur->right` is captured before anything is released; key freed; `value_free` called while `cur` is still readable; node `rb_free`d in heap mode only. Rotate branch: `cur->left = left->right` re-homes β *before* `left->right = cur` overwrites its only link (swapping those two lines makes `cur` its own left child). No recursion, no allocation, no auxiliary stack; `-fstack-usage` reports a fixed 32-byte frame. Parent pointers, colors, `t->root` and `t->size` go stale during the walk and are never read, which is why red-black violations mid-teardown are harmless: the loop depends only on left/right reachability. `pool_destroy` runs after the walk (which reads node fields living inside slabs) and before `rb_free(t)` (which is where `t->pool` is read). The only code change to `rb_destroy` is a one-line invariant comment above the loop. (2) **Slice 1 (`45f8171`).** Three test hooks under `RBTREE_TEST_HOOKS`, none in the frozen header. `rb_test_make_spine(t, left)` reshapes a tree into a single left or right spine using the *real* `rotate_left`/`rotate_right`, so parent pointers, `t->root`, size, in-order sequence and ownership survive. `rb_test_spine_len` measures the spine independently. `rb_test_links_ok` checks every child→parent link, that the root's parent is NULL, strict in-order and count == size; it is an iterative parent-pointer walk that only climbs links it verified on the way down. Six new teardown tests run in both modes (empty-with-destructor, single, balanced 127, irregular 600-op LCG insert/overwrite/delete, left spine 64, right spine 64). Each destroys with `fault_alloc_arm(1)` and asserts `fault_alloc_total() == 0` plus an exact `value_free` count. Fixed the stale comment on `test_destroy_left_heavy_chain`, which claimed e,d,c,b,a builds a left chain; since the HW1 fixup it builds `d(b(a,c),e)`, which the Reach rotates 3 times. (3) **Slice 2 (`8c24b06`).** `test_rbtree --stress N` covers {heap, pooled} × {balanced, left spine}. The tree is built and checked on the main thread (`rb_validate` + `links_ok` for balanced; `spine_len == N` + `links_ok` for the spine). Then a pthread with a stack size of exactly 64 KB (set and read back via `getstacksize`) runs `rb_foreach` (balanced only) and `rb_destroy`. After join the harness asserts 0 `rb_malloc` calls, foreach visited N keys in strictly increasing order, and every per-key hit counter equals 1, reporting missed and repeated separately. Makefile: a shared `SAN_FLAGS`; `-pthread` on the unit binary only; `make test` runs `--stress 20000`; new opt-in `make stress-asan` (clean, ASan/UBSan sub-make, `--stress 1000000`) using the same clean-then-recursive-make structure as `asan`; `make memcheck` adds `valgrind ... --stress 20000`.
PROOF (termination and correctness of the teardown loop): Let F be the nodes already released and R the nodes reachable from `cur` via left/right links. Loop invariant at the top of each pass: (I1) R is a binary tree rooted at `cur`, and R and F partition the original nodes; (I2) no left/right field in R points into F; (I3) R's in-order sequence is the original sequence minus F, and F is a *prefix* of it (nodes are freed in ascending key order); (I4) each node in F had its key freed once, `value_free` called once, and (heap mode) its node freed once, while nothing in R has; (I5) `t`, `value_free` and `pool` are live, while root/size/parent/color are stale and unread. A rotation keeps the node set and in-order sequence (`(A L β) cur C` = `A L (β cur C)`) and frees nothing. A free removes `cur`, which has no left child and is therefore R's minimum (so F stays a prefix) and is R's root (so nothing in R′ points to it); `next` was captured first. At exit `cur == NULL`, so R = ∅ and F is everything. **Measure:** Φ = 2N − S, with N = |R| and S = the length of the right spine from `cur`. Φ ≥ N ≥ 0 because S ≤ N. *Rotate:* N is unchanged and S grows by exactly 1 (the new spine is L, cur, then the old spine below cur), so Φ falls by exactly 1. *Free:* N falls by 1 and S falls by exactly 1 (the root was the head of the spine and the rest of the spine is `next`'s spine), so 2N falls by 2 and S by 1, and Φ falls by exactly 1. Hence the loop runs exactly Φ₀ = 2n − s₀ passes: n − s₀ rotations and n frees, linear time. Checked on an instrumented scratch copy of the real loop: iterations == 2n − s₀ with zero steps whose ΔΦ ≠ −1, for n = 1, 2, 7, 1000 and 10^5. Worked example on the perfect tree 4(2(1,3),6(5,7)), n = 7, s₀ = 3, Φ₀ = 11: rotate@4 (10), rotate@2 (9), free 1 (8), free 2 (7), rotate@4 (6), free 3 (5), free 4 (4), rotate@6 (3), free 5 (2), free 6 (1), free 7 (0). That is 4 rotations = n − s₀ and 7 frees, in ascending order.
RESULTS: Default run 3371 assertions, 0 FAIL; heap 1374 / pooled 1350, delta still 24, and all 1302 non-sweep descriptions are identical across modes (both modes grew by exactly 737: 29 new M3 assertions plus `make_int` fixture lines). `make test` ~1.9 s, `make asan` ~6.2 s, `make stress-asan` ~5.8 s (34/34 PASS at N = 10^6: foreach visited all 10^6 keys in order, 0 missed and 0 repeated destructor calls in all four cases), `make memcheck` ~6.5 s (four runs, all "All heap blocks were freed", 0 errors; the stress run did 120,484 allocs/frees). Scratch-only measurements: ASan peak RSS at 10^6 ≈ 134 MB heap / 121 MB pooled; the full 10^6 case is also valgrind-clean (≈ 8.5 s heap, 6.5 s pooled per case) but was not made routine. `rb_test_make_spine` is linear: exactly 2n − s₀ passes and n − s₀ rotations at every n from 1.25·10^5 to 2·10^6, with 1M nodes in 0.036 s (0.05–0.06 s under ASan).
NEGATIVE CONTROL (does the stress test detect recursion?): in a scratch copy I replaced `rb_destroy` with a textbook post-order recursive free and ran the real harness under ASan. The balanced case **passed** at both N = 2·10^4 and N = 10^6 (height ≈ 40 fits in 64 KB), and the left-spine case died with `AddressSanitizer: stack-overflow ... in rec_free` at both sizes. So the spec's own required test (a balanced 10^6-node destroy on a 64 KB stack) cannot distinguish recursive from iterative teardown on its own; the hook-built spine is what makes the test discriminating, and even the routine 2·10^4 size catches it. The control lives in scratch only; it is not in the repo.
MUTATION CHECKS on the slice-1 tests (scratch copies under ASan): dropping `value_free` in destroy → 14 FAILs plus a LeakSanitizer report; an `rb_malloc` inside destroy → 12 FAILs; pooled destroy also `rb_free`ing nodes → ASan double-free; `make_spine` doing nothing → 4 FAILs; stopping one rotation early → 2 FAILs; one stale parent pointer after reshaping → 4 FAILs (`links_ok`); swapping the two rotation lines → infinite loop (caught only by a timeout, not an assertion). Slice-2 failure paths forced in scratch: `pthread_attr_init` failure, `pthread_create` failure, an insert failing mid-build, and `make_tree` failing each report FAIL with no ASan/leak findings; a forced `pthread_join` failure aborts by design.
DECIDED: (1) **No production teardown change.** The review and proof found no defect, so pointer reversal was not considered further. (2) **Test hooks, not a test-only API.** Reshaping must use the real rotations so parent pointers stay correct (Evening 8 may walk them), and the spine is only reachable through a hook because `rb_insert`/`rb_delete` keep height O(log n). (3) **The reshape never vouches for itself.** The first draft had `make_spine` return its own spine length; a "does nothing, returns n" mutant passed, so measuring moved into a separate `rb_test_spine_len`. (4) **Build outside the thread.** Only foreach/destroy run on the 64 KB stack, so a crash there is attributable to them; `rb_validate` (recursive, height-bounded) stays on the main thread. (5) **Exact destructor accounting via hit counters, not 10^6 value mallocs.** This catches missed, repeated and stray calls exactly. (6) **Opt-in million, routine 2·10^4.** `stress-asan` is its own target so `make test` stays ~2 s; `make test` still runs `--stress 20000` so `make asan` exercises the harness every time. Valgrind uses 2·10^4. This is a deliberate shrink for runtime, and REFLECTION.md will say so. Scratch-only measurements: ASan peak RSS at 10^6 ≈ 134 MB heap / 121 MB pooled; the full 10^6 case is also valgrind-clean (≈ 8.5 s heap, 6.5 s pooled per case) but was not made routine. `rb_test_make_spine` is linear: exactly 2n − s₀ passes and n − s₀ rotations at every n from 1.25·10^5 to 2·10^6, with 1M nodes in 0.036 s (0.05–0.06 s under ASan).

-NEGATIVE CONTROL (does the stress test detect recursion?): in a scratch copy I replaced `rb_destroy` with a textbook post-order recursive free and ran the real harness under ASan. The balanced case **passed** at both N = 2·10^4 and N = 10^6 (height ≈ 40 fits in 64 KB), and the left-spine case died with `AddressSanitizer: stack-overflow ... in rec_free` at both sizes. So the spec's own required test (a balanced 10^6-node destroy on a 64 KB stack) cannot distinguish recursive from iterative teardown on its own; the hook-built spine is what makes the test discriminating, and even the routine 2·10^4 size catches it. The control lives in scratch only; it is not in the repo.

+NEGATIVE CONTROL (does the stress test detect recursion?): in a scratch copy I replaced `rb_destroy` with a textbook post-order recursive free and ran the real harness under ASan. The heap balanced case **passed** (thread joined, every destructor called once) at both N = 2·10^4 and N = 10^6, because height ≈ 40 fits in 64 KB. The heap left-spine case that follows it then died with `AddressSanitizer: stack-overflow ... in rec_free` at both sizes. The abort ends the process, so the pooled cases never ran in the control. So the spec's own required test (a balanced 10^6-node destroy on a 64 KB stack) cannot distinguish recursive from iterative teardown on its own; the hook-built spine is what makes the test discriminating, and even the routine 2·10^4 size catches it. The control lives in scratch only; it is not in the repo.

MUTATION CHECKS on the slice-1 tests (scratch copies under ASan): dropping `value_free` in destroy → 14 FAILs plus a LeakSanitizer report; an `rb_malloc` inside destroy → 12 FAILs; pooled destroy also `rb_free`ing nodes → ASan double-free; `make_spine` doing nothing → 4 FAILs; stopping one rotation early → 2 FAILs; one stale parent pointer after reshaping → 4 FAILs (`links_ok`); swapping the two rotation lines → infinite loop (caught only by a timeout, not an assertion). Slice-2 failure paths forced in scratch: `pthread_attr_init` failure, `pthread_create` failure, an insert failing mid-build, and `make_tree` failing each report FAIL with no ASan/leak findings; a forced `pthread_join` failure aborts by design.

DECIDED: (1) **No production teardown change.** The review and proof found no defect, so pointer reversal was not considered further. (2) **Test hooks, not a test-only API.** Reshaping must use the real rotations so parent pointers stay correct (Evening 8 may walk them), and the spine is only reachable through a hook because `rb_insert`/`rb_delete` keep height O(log n). (3) **The reshape never vouches for itself.** The first draft had `make_spine` return its own spine length; a "does nothing, returns n" mutant passed, so measuring moved into a separate `rb_test_spine_len`. (4) **Build outside the thread.** Only foreach/destroy run on the 64 KB stack, so a crash there is attributable to them; `rb_validate` (recursive, height-bounded) stays on the main thread. (5) **Exact destructor accounting via hit counters, not 10^6 value mallocs.** This catches missed, repeated and stray calls exactly. (6) **Opt-in million, routine 2·10^4.** `stress-asan` is its own target so `make test` stays ~2 s; `make test` still runs `--stress 20000` so `make asan` exercises the harness every time. Valgrind uses 2·10^4. This is a deliberate shrink for runtime, and REFLECTION.md will say so. (7) **One `SAN_FLAGS`**, so `asan` and `stress-asan` cannot drift; the expanded `asan` command is byte-identical to before. (8) **Line-buffered stdout in `--stress` mode only**, because the negative control showed that an ASan abort lost every PASS line when stdout went to a file, so a CI log could not say which case crashed. (9) **Abort on a failed join.** A created-but-unjoined worker may still own the tree, the counters and the injector's counter, so there is nothing safe to read, free or disarm. `pthread_attr_destroy` runs only if `pthread_attr_init` succeeded.

LEARNED: The sharpest point was that a passing stress test is not evidence of the property it is named after: a red-black tree's height bound means the spec's balanced 10^6-node test passes a recursive teardown, and only the positive control made that visible. Second, a measure that drops by *exactly* one per pass gives more than termination: it gives the exact pass count (2n − s₀), which turned the proof into something I could check numerically against the real loop. Third, two small harness lessons: a test hook that reports on its own work hides its own bugs (mutant M5), and buffered stdout under an abort silently deletes the evidence of where a crash happened.

content.text:
Slice 2 is committed as **`8c24b06`** (`M3: million-node 64KB-stack teardown stress harness`). It changes `Makefile` and `tests/test_rbtree.c` (+184 / −6). After it the working tree was clean and `main` was 2 commits ahead of `origin/main`, not pushed. Evening 8 is not started.

## Final review before that commit

**1. Failure-path cleanup: two real defects, both fixed before committing.**
- **Uninitialized attribute:** `pthread_attr_destroy` ran even when `pthread_attr_init` had failed. It now runs only if init succeeded.
- **Failed join:** if `pthread_join` failed after a successful create, the harness went on to read and free the hit counters, and read and disarm the allocation counter, while the worker might still be running. My first fix still left that counter race, so the final version reports FAIL and aborts before touching anything shared.
- **Forced in scratch copies under ASan with leak checking**, every path behaves:

  | Forced failure | Outcome |
  |---|---|
  | `pthread_attr_init` | FAIL lines, no ASan or leak reports |
  | `pthread_create` | FAIL lines; the main thread reclaims the tree and every value is still freed exactly once |
  | Insert fails mid-build | FAIL lines, no ASan or leak reports |
  | `make_tree` returns NULL | FAIL lines, no ASan or leak reports |
  | `pthread_join` | Aborts as designed (exit code 134) |

**2. Makefile:** no duplicate rules or flags.
- `asan` and `stress-asan` each appear twice, but that's one flag-setting line plus one rule each.
- The sanitizer flags are defined once, in `SAN_FLAGS`.
- The second `-pthread` match is the comment text "64 KB-pthread-stack", not a flag.
- `make -n` shows `asan`, `stress-asan` and `memcheck` all still start with `rm -rf build` and then a sub-make.
- The `Error 141` I saw came from piping `make -n` into `head`. Without the pipe it exits 0.

**3. Production code:** `git diff HEAD -- src include` was empty before this commit. `rb_destroy` and `rb_foreach` have had no executable changes this evening; only the invariant comment was added.

**4. Checks re-run after the fixes:**
- `git diff --check` clean.
- `make test`, `make asan`, `make stress-asan` (34/34 PASS at 10⁶) and `make memcheck` (4 runs, each 0 errors and all heap blocks freed) all pass.
- The normal run still shows heap 1374, pooled 1350, a gap of 24.

## Documentation changes, not committed, waiting for your review

`git status` shows `M CLAUDE.md` (+42 / −22) and `M DEVLOG.md` (+12). The full diff is in the output above.

**CLAUDE.md:**
- The "As of" paragraph is now dated 2026-10-12, with the four gates and their numbers:
  - 3371 assertions in a normal run;
  - 34 in the stress harness at both N = 20,000 and N = 10⁶;
  - the fourth valgrind run, with 120,484 allocations and frees;
  - a note that valgrind runs the smaller 20,000 case on purpose.
- The coverage paragraph now says 1374 vs 1350 and 1302 assertions shared by both modes. I recomputed the old 565 from commit `8cd7c72` with the same method. Both modes grew by exactly 737, and the sweep is unchanged, so the gap of 24 still comes entirely from the sweep.
- The build-command block and test-binary usage now cover `--stress N`, `stress-asan`, and the four-run `memcheck`.
- One status line says Mutation 3's teardown half is done (`45f8171`, `8c24b06`). The code map and the destroy-coverage summary mention the new hooks and tests.

**DEVLOG.md:** one Evening 7 entry in the existing STATE/DID/DECIDED/LEARNED/NEXT/OPEN format, plus PROOF, RESULTS, NEGATIVE CONTROL and MUTATION CHECKS sections.
- **Proof:** the invariant (I1–I5), and Φ = 2N − S with the reason Φ drops by exactly 1 for both a rotation and a free. That gives exactly 2n − s₀ passes, checked numerically, plus the 7-node walkthrough.
- **Results:** both slices, timings, and the million-node numbers.
- **Negative control:** I re-ran the recursive teardown control with the line-buffered harness before writing this section, and it confirms the balanced case passes at both 20,000 and 10⁶. The left-only chain case dies with `stack-overflow` at both sizes. One caveat is written into the entry: that abort ends the process, so only heap mode was observed and the pooled cases never ran.
- **Open items:** carried into OPEN, including the REFLECTION.md notes still owed and the three CLAUDE.md/spec mismatches I did *not* fix (`rb_snapshot` "graded", "≥8 commits", "recursion permitted (§9)").
- **Session length:** missing from the heading. Add it if you want it, since I don't know it.

Proposed commit message, following the M2 docs commit `2dc65e3`:
`M3: devlog and CLAUDE.md state for O(1)-space teardown`

Tell me whether to commit the documentation as it is or with changes.

`CS370-HW2.pdf`, a continuation of HW1). `include/rbtree.h` is the frozen contract — it was
re-frozen for HW2 and now also declares `rb_create_pooled` (Mutation 2: node storage drawn
from an internal slab pool) and `rb_snapshot` (Mutation 4: O(1) copy-on-write snapshot, "The
Reach" — no longer just ungraded prep, see below). `rb_create_pooled` is now implemented
(commit `3d1afa9`); `rb_snapshot` is not. `NOTES.md`
contains the assignment spec, the design decisions already made (including a devlog of the
  child, and the mirrored (right-child-of-right-child) symmetry of every fixup case — the
  spec explicitly calls out the mirror image as "the half people forget."
- **`rb_foreach` / `rb_destroy`**: recursion is permitted for this assignment (spec §9). See
  "The Reach" below for the ungraded non-recursive teardown.
- **`rb_validate` invariants** (must detect and report *which* invariant broke):
  1. root is black
## The Reach — HW1 (ungraded) vs HW2 (`rb_snapshot`, in scope)

HW1 framed non-recursive, O(1)-auxiliary-space teardown as ungraded prep for "the next
assignment" (spec §10, "The Reach") — that next assignment is this one. `rb_destroy`'s
rotate-into-a-right-spine-while-freeing technique already exists in `src/rbtree.c` from HW1;
HW2's frozen header now adds `rb_snapshot` (Mutation 4: O(1) copy-on-write snapshot, NULL on
allocation failure), which is graded here and is not yet implemented. Treat any reuse of the
Reach technique for `rb_snapshot` as a new, from-scratch design question, not a copy-paste of
`rb_destroy` — check CS370-HW2.pdf's own section for `rb_snapshot` before attempting it, and
CS370-HW1.pdf §10 for the original Reach writeup.

## Process requirements / deliverables (spec §7, §15, §17)

These are graded independently of the code and must not be neglected or bulk-generated at the end:

- **Git history**: ≥ 8 meaningful commits tracking the milestones (M0–M3 in the schedule table,
  spec §5 — `M<n>: <what>` in a commit message names the milestone, not a "Mutation"). A single
  "final submission" commit is an automatic process-grade of zero.

DECIDED: (1) **No production teardown change.** The review and proof found no defect, so pointer reversal was not considered further. (2) **Test hooks, not a test-only API.** Reshaping must use the real rotations so parent pointers stay correct (Evening 8 may walk them), and the spine is only reachable through a hook because `rb_insert`/`rb_delete` keep height O(log n). (3) **The reshape never vouches for itself.** The first draft had `make_spine` return its own spine length; a "does nothing, returns n" mutant passed, so measuring moved into a separate `rb_test_spine_len`. (4) **Build outside the thread.** Only foreach/destroy run on the 64 KB stack, so a crash there is attributable to them; `rb_validate` (recursive, height-bounded) stays on the main thread. (5) **Exact destructor accounting via hit counters, not 10^6 value mallocs.** This catches missed, repeated and stray calls exactly. (6) **Opt-in million, routine 2·10^4.** `stress-asan` is its own target so `make test` stays ~2 s; `make test` still runs `--stress 20000` so `make asan` exercises the harness every time. Valgrind uses 2·10^4. This is a deliberate shrink for runtime, and REFLECTION.md will say so. (7) **One `SAN_FLAGS`**, so `asan` and `stress-asan` cannot drift; the expanded `asan` command is byte-identical to before. (8) **Line-buffered stdout in `--stress` mode only**, because the negative control showed that an ASan abort lost every PASS line when stdout went to a file, so a CI log could not say which case crashed. (9) **Abort on a failed join.** A created-but-unjoined worker may still own the tree, the counters and the injector's counter, so there is nothing safe to read, free or disarm. `pthread_attr_destroy` runs only if `pthread_attr_init` succeeded.

Second, a measure that drops by *exactly* one per pass gives more than termination: it gives the exact pass count (2n − s₀), which turned the proof into something I could check numerically against the real loop. Third, two small harness lessons: a test hook that reports on its own work hides its own bugs (mutant M5), and buffered stdout under an abort silently deletes the evidence of where a crash happened.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**
   - **Overall task:** CS370 HW2, Evening 7, Mutation 3: O(1)-space teardown.
     - Keep the existing iterative right-spine `rb_destroy`; do not redesign it unless a correctness defect turns up. None did.
     - Prove termination with the measure Φ = 2N − S.
     - Add tests for both heap and pooled trees.
     - Add a million-node stress test on a 64 KB pthread stack that runs under ASan.
     - Work in two slices, with a review before each commit.
   - **User decisions along the way:**
     - Approved a hook that exists only under `RBTREE_TEST_HOOKS` and is never exposed in `rbtree.h`.
     - The million-node case is opt-in.
     - `make test` runs `--stress 20000`.
     - The new target is named `stress-asan`, and the sanitizer flags are shared through `SAN_FLAGS`.
     - Valgrind runs the 20,000-node case.
     - Do not run the recursive `rb_foreach` on the million-node left spine yet (Evening 8).
     - Exact invariant comment wording: `/* Invariant: cur reaches N unfreed nodes; 2*N-S decreases (S = right-spine length). */`
     - The DEVLOG entry and CLAUDE.md count updates were deferred until after slice 2.
     - The user asked for three CLAUDE.md corrections against the HW2 spec, listed below.
     - The Evening 7 DEVLOG entry stays as written, including the Φ proof and the qualified negative-control results. Do not invent a session duration.
   - **Latest request:** after committing the docs, report the commit hash and git status, and report whether main is ahead of origin/main, "since we need to push the completed work before proceeding." The user said "Do not begin Evening 8 yet."

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Red-black tree in C23 with parent pointers. The `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` seam and the fault injector, where `fault_alloc_arm(1)` plus `fault_alloc_total()==0` checks that nothing was allocated.
   - Slab pool: pooled teardown frees only keys and values, then `pool_destroy` releases the slabs wholesale.
   - Right-spine "Reach" teardown.
     - Invariants I1–I5.
     - Measure Φ = 2N − S, which drops by exactly 1 on every pass, so teardown takes exactly 2n − s₀ passes: n − s₀ rotations and n frees.
   - pthread with a 64 KB stack, ASan/UBSan, valgrind.
   - A balanced tree is about 40 levels deep, which is shallow enough that a recursive teardown would still pass the balanced test, so the test cannot detect recursion. The left-spine shape is what detects it.
   - Mutation testing used scratch copies of the source.
   - The Makefile keeps its clean-then-recursive-make sequencing.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**
   - **`src/rbtree.c`** (commit 45f8171):
     - Adds the one-line invariant comment above the `rb_destroy` loop. This is the only change to production code.
     - Adds three hooks under `#ifdef RBTREE_TEST_HOOKS`:
       - `void rb_test_make_spine(rbtree_t *t, bool left)`, iterative, using the real `rotate_left`/`rotate_right`;
       - `size_t rb_test_spine_len(const rbtree_t *t, bool left)`;
       - `bool rb_test_links_ok(const rbtree_t *t)`, an iterative parent-pointer walk that checks child→parent links, root parent NULL, strict in-order and count == size.
   - **`tests/test_rbtree.c`**:
     - **Commit 45f8171:**
       - extern declarations for the hooks;
       - a fixed stale comment in `test_destroy_left_heavy_chain` (the tree is actually d(b(a,c),e), with 3 rotations);
       - helpers `destroy_and_check`, `build_scrambled` (stride 37, `char key[24]`), and `struct sorted_ctx`/`check_sorted`;
       - tests `test_destroy_empty_with_destructor`, `_single_with_destructor`, `_balanced` (127), `_irregular` (600-operation LCG), and `_left_spine`/`_right_spine` (64), all added to `run_tree_suite`.
     - **Commit 8c24b06:** adds `#include <pthread.h>` and the stress harness:
       - `STRESS_STACK_SIZE` and `STRESS_MAX_N` (10⁸);
       - `stress_value_free` (hit counters), `struct stress_job`, `stress_thread`, `gcd_ul`, `stress_case(n, left_spine)`, `run_stress`;
       - `main(int argc, char **argv)` parses `--stress N`, exits 2 on bad arguments, and calls `setvbuf(stdout, NULL, _IOLBF, 0)` in stress mode;
       - failure paths: `pthread_attr_destroy` only if init succeeded; abort if join fails; `rb_destroy` on the main thread if create fails.

CC := gcc
CFLAGS := -std=c23 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -g -O1 -Iinclude -Itests
# TEST_CFLAGS is recursively expanded (=, not :=) so it picks up the
# asan target's target-specific `CFLAGS +=` override at build time.
TEST_CFLAGS = $(CFLAGS) -DRBTREE_TEST_HOOKS
# One definition shared by `asan` and `stress-asan`, so the two can't drift.
SAN_FLAGS := -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer
SRC := src/rbtree.c src/pool.c
TSRC := tests/test_rbtree.c
FAULT_SRC := tests/fault_alloc.c
FAULT_HDR := tests/fault_alloc.h
BIN := build/test_rbtree
FUZZBIN := build/fuzz

all: $(BIN) $(FUZZBIN)

$(BIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) $(FAULT_SRC) $(FAULT_HDR) include/rbtree.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(TEST_CFLAGS) $(SRC) $(TSRC) $(FAULT_SRC) -pthread -o $@

$(FUZZBIN): $(SRC) tests/fuzz.c $(FAULT_SRC) $(FAULT_HDR) include/rbtree.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) tests/fuzz.c $(FAULT_SRC) -o $@

# The fuzzer runs the full op count in BOTH node-storage modes: a pooled tree
# that has not been fuzzed as hard as the heap one is not covered. "-" keeps
# the default time(NULL) seeding in both passes. `--stress 20000` runs the
# Mutation 3 64 KB-pthread-stack teardown harness at a routine size; the
# 10^6-node case is opt-in via `stress-asan` below.
test: $(BIN) $(FUZZBIN)
	./$(BIN) && ./$(BIN) --stress 20000 && \
		./$(FUZZBIN) 100000 - heap && ./$(FUZZBIN) 100000 - pooled

# Both gates rebuild from scratch, and the order must be GUARANTEED rather
# than incidental. So `clean` is the sole prerequisite of each and the build
# is driven by a recursive $(MAKE) in the recipe.
#
# Why not `asan: clean test` / `memcheck: clean all`: those name siblings,
# and -j is free to run them concurrently -- `clean` can delete build/ after
# the other populated it, or race it mid-compile. Even serially, make decides
# whether `test`/`all` is up to date from the binaries present when it builds
# its dependency graph, which immediately after a `make asan` are the
# ASan-instrumented ones.
#
# For memcheck that produced a gate which passed having tested nothing:
# valgrind over an ASan-built binary reports "0 allocs, 0 frees" and "All
# heap blocks were freed -- no leaks are possible", so --error-exitcode=1
# never fires and the run reads as success. One prerequisite plus an ordered
# recipe makes clean-then-build the only possible sequence at any -j.
#
# asan hands its effective CFLAGS to the sub-make explicitly. The
# target-specific `+=` below IS in scope inside asan's own recipe, so
# $(CFLAGS) there is already the augmented value; passing it as a command-line
# assignment is what carries it across the recursive invocation, where the
# `asan` target is never visited and its `+=` would therefore never apply.
# TEST_CFLAGS stays recursively expanded (=, not :=) so the hooks build picks
# the sanitizer flags up too.
asan: CFLAGS += $(SAN_FLAGS)
asan: clean
	$(MAKE) test CFLAGS="$(CFLAGS)"

# Opt-in Mutation 3 gate: 10^6-node teardown (and balanced foreach) on a 64 KB
# pthread stack under ASan/UBSan. Same clean-then-recursive-make structure as
# asan above, for the same reasons; it builds only the unit binary it runs.
stress-asan: CFLAGS += $(SAN_FLAGS)
stress-asan: clean
	$(MAKE) $(BIN) CFLAGS="$(CFLAGS)"
	./$(BIN) --stress 1000000

memcheck: clean
	$(MAKE) all
	valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all \
		--error-exitcode=1 ./$(BIN)
	valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all \
		--error-exitcode=1 ./$(FUZZBIN) 20000 - heap
	valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all \
		--error-exitcode=1 ./$(FUZZBIN) 20000 - pooled
	valgrind --leak-check=full --show-leak-kinds=all \
		--error-exitcode=1 ./$(BIN) --stress 20000
clean:
	rm -rf build

.PHONY: all test asan stress-asan memcheck clean

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>
